subject: HEXOS-6 (CONDITIONAL): Hex Live bootable image, justified ONLY by hardware labs
description:
Debian/Ubuntu respin, session = the shell, lab tooling preinstalled. The ONLY justification is hardware a browser cannot reach: WiFi Arsenal monitor mode, Signal toolkit USB/serial/SDR. STATED COST: a distro carries a years-long security-update obligation. Do not start before HEXOS-0/1/3/5.
[2026-09-06 02:17] RE-VOTE 2026-09-05 after the distributed-compute-fabric brief surfaced. Q1 (what is the image FOR): A UNCHANGED, 4-0 (Nancy switched C->A, Chris A, Mallory D which is A-for-shipping, primary A). Fabric/node-agent treated as a SEPARATE project needing its own threat model and panel vote. Reasons converged independently: the brief is a conversation record not a spec; there is no lab network so there is no pool to control; and Mallory established the disqualifying one, that no isolation exists between a fabric job and the root-capable student session this image deliberately creates for monitor mode. I also had to retract an inference: I cited bc1's lab-manager as proof Phase 2/3 exist, and Nancy correctly called it collapsing two trust models. It is a session manager on ONE trusted host, not evidence a fabric enrolling untrusted student machines is nearly built. Q2 (what does it land on): SPLIT. Nancy and Chris wanted a provisioned kiosk identity; Mallory voted against because a credential baked into a distributable image is readable via strings/dd/root and re-creates the hexworth_tenant forgery class on disk. Resolved to Chris's OTHER option, which survives her objection: an explicit LOGIN at boot. login.html already takes ?return=, so the kiosk lands on login and hands off to /hex/. No credential in the image, and an already-sorted student reaches their own shell. Implemented in _tools/hexos-live/build.sh; rebuilding and will re-verify by QEMU screendump.
